journal_name: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence

abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a unified information-theoretic framework that fundamentally reconceptualizes pattern recognition theory. Traditional approaches in statistical pattern recognition rely on restrictive distributional assumptions that limit their applicability across diverse data modalities. The proposed framework establishes rigorous connections between information theory, learning theory, and classifier design through a common mathematical foundation based on Renyi entropy and f-divergence measures. We prove that optimal decision boundaries can be characterized exclusively through information-theoretic quantities, eliminating the need for explicit density estimation in high-dimensional spaces. The framework provides a new theoretical lens for understanding the relationships among feature selection, neural network architecture design, and generalization performance. By reformulating the pattern recognition problem as an information transmission optimization, we derive novel bounds on the Bayes error rate that are tighter than existing results. This paradigm shift enables the development of classification methods that are both theoretically grounded and computationally tractable. Experiments on synthetic and benchmark datasets demonstrate that classifiers designed within this unified framework achieve superior performance compared to conventional approaches while providing theoretical guarantees that were previously unavailable. The framework opens new research directions for both artificial intelligence theory and practical pattern recognition applications.

This paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of feature selection in deep neural networks for pattern recognition tasks, addressing a critical gap between empirical success and theoretical understanding. While deep learning has achieved remarkable success across computer vision and data mining applications, the theoretical mechanisms underlying effective feature selection remain poorly characterized. We introduce a novel analysis framework based on 马尔可夫随机游走 dynamics and spectral graph theory to characterize feature importance in neural architectures. Our analysis reveals that existing gradient-based selection criteria systematically underestimate feature interactions in high-dimensional data, leading to suboptimal classifier performance. We prove that optimal feature subsets exhibit a concentration property around a theoretical threshold that depends on the data manifold structure. Building on these insights, we propose a theoretically motivated feature selection criterion with improved statistical guarantees for multi-class classification. Our analysis provides non-asymptotic bounds on the estimation error, demonstrating that the proposed selector achieves near-minimax optimal rates under mild regularity conditions. The theoretical framework reveals a fundamental trade-off between feature efficiency and classification accuracy that has not been previously characterized. Experimental validation on high-dimensional datasets confirms the theoretical predictions, with the proposed approach consistently outperforming alternatives.

This paper presents a novel neuro-symbolic architecture for visual reasoning tasks that fundamentally integrates deep learning with symbolic artificial intelligence. Existing approaches in computer vision typically employ end-to-end neural networks that function as black boxes, lacking the interpretability and logical reasoning capabilities required for complex AI applications. Our system introduces a differentiable logic programming layer that bridges convolutional neural networks for image understanding with symbolic knowledge representation and reasoning. The architecture enables joint end-to-end training across perception and reasoning modules, representing a paradigm shift from traditional pipeline approaches. We design novel operator abstractions that maintain semantic consistency between neural feature representations and logical predicates while allowing gradient-based optimization. The system architecture incorporates a memory-augmented reasoning component that enables handling of novel visual concepts through symbolic inference. Experimental evaluation on complex visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrates that the proposed architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance while providing interpretable logical explanations for predictions. Ablation studies validate the complementary contributions of neural and symbolic components, confirming that this integration paradigm offers capabilities beyond what either component can achieve independently. The work establishes a new direction for artificial intelligence systems that combine the pattern recognition strengths of deep learning with the logical reasoning capabilities of symbolic AI.

This paper presents an efficient attention-based framework for real-time computer vision applications, incorporating hierarchical attention mechanisms and optimized inference pipelines. While attention mechanisms have demonstrated remarkable success across image processing and computer vision tasks, their computational overhead remains prohibitive for real-time deployment on resource-constrained platforms. We introduce a multi-scale attention module that dynamically adjusts computational allocation based on scene complexity, achieving a favorable trade-off between recognition accuracy and inference speed. The system architecture integrates lightweight backbone networks with novel attention refinement layers designed specifically for efficient deployment. A progressive training strategy with attention-aware regularization improves model convergence and robustness across diverse imaging conditions. The framework includes a quantized inference engine that reduces memory footprint and computational requirements while maintaining accuracy within acceptable bounds. Extensive evaluation on standard benchmarks demonstrates significant improvements in both throughput and accuracy compared to existing efficient designs. The system achieves real-time performance exceeding 30 frames per second on embedded hardware while delivering competitive accuracy on challenging object detection and image classification tasks. We provide comprehensive analysis of the attention mechanism's impact on different computer vision tasks and demonstrate the framework's generalizability across multiple application domains in artificial intelligence.
